title: Application Metrics and Tracing knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Application Metrics and Tracing?
options: Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Check both node and npm versions, commit the lockfile, and document the exact project commands.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
questions.answer_key: Check both node and npm versions, commit the lockfile, and document the exact project commands.
questions.explanation: Check both node and npm versions, commit the lockfile, and document the exact project commands. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Application Metrics and Tracing?
questions.explanation: “Request counts and durations” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Application Metrics and Tracing implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
